question: Dalchand Sharma is an eminent Pakhawaj exponent of which of the following gharanas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nathdwara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dalchand Sharma is a renowned exponent of the **Pakhawaj**, a traditional Indian percussion instrument.
 
• He is associated with the **Nathdwara Gharana**, which is famous for its tradition of Pakhawaj playing.
 
• The Nathdwara Gharana has its roots in the temple town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan and is deeply influenced by the **Vaishnavite devotional music traditions.**
 
• Dalchand Sharma has contributed significantly to preserving and popularizing the Pakhawaj through performances and teaching.
 
• The **Pakhawaj** is a barrel-shaped drum that is primarily used in Hindustani classical music and accompanies genres like **Dhrupad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakhawaj**

 
 
• The Pakhawaj is a traditional Indian percussion instrument, known for its deep, resonant sound.
 
• It is an ancient drum that predates the tabla and is closely associated with the **Dhrupad** style of Hindustani classical music.
 
• The Pakhawaj is played using both hands, with specific strokes producing distinct tones on either side of the drum.
 
• Its construction involves a wooden barrel body with leather drum heads on both sides, tuned using leather straps.
 
 
 
• **Nathdwara Gharana**
 
 
• This gharana is named after the temple town of Nathdwara in Rajasthan.
 
• It is known for its association with the **devotional music of the Pushtimarg sect**, dedicated to Lord Krishna.
 
• Artists of this gharana specialize in Pakhawaj playing and maintain a rich tradition of rhythmic compositions.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest genres of Hindustani classical music, emphasizing spiritual and meditative aspects.
 
• It is characterized by slow, deliberate movements and the use of the Pakhawaj for rhythmic accompaniment.
 
• This style is often performed in temples and has a strong connection to India's cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Gharanas in Music**
 
 
• A gharana represents a specific school or style of classical music, passed down through generations.
 
• Each gharana is unique in its approach to melody, rhythm, and technique.
 
• Gharanas play a crucial role in preserving the diversity and richness of Indian classical music traditions.
